To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the polarized antiquark asymmetry Delta_ub(x) - Delta_db(x) is positive, in contrast to the unpolarized asymmetry dbar(x) = ubar(x); and (2) the polarized asymmetries Delta_ubar(x), Delta_db(x) are large at x < 0.1, and are dominated by the pion cloud contribution.

the pion cloud is the dominant effect in the polarized asymmetries of the anti-quark flavor distributions, and that this effect is of a similar size as the Pauli blocking effect in the unpolarized asymmetries.

(i) the polarized antiquark flavor asymmetry can qualitatively explained by Pauli blocking, (ii) the Pauli blocking effect is not present for the unpolarized asymmetry, but (iii) a large positive polarized antiquark asymmetry is obtained in the meson picture from pi-N -sigma-N interference-type contributions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of how the nucleon structure emerges from the quark and gluon degrees of freedom, and how this picture relates to the mesonic structure of the nucleon, which is the natural language of low energy hadronic phenomena.
the flavor dependence of the polarized antiquark distributions.
the question how much the proton's spin is carried by the quark spin and by the orbital angular momentum of its quarks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pauli blocking and the pion cloud picture both are valid, but in a complementary way, i.e., the Pauli blocking effect is dominant at low x, whereas the pion cloud dominates the high x region.
the Pauli blocking effect is not large enough to explain the flavor asymmetry of Delta_ubar(x), and that the polarized antiquark distributions are mainly due to meson cloud effects.
the flavor asymmetry of polarized antiquarks is large and positive, but the origin of this asymmetry is not yet understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flavor asymmetry of both unpolarized and polarized antiquark distributions is a consequence of the chiral structure of the nucleon, which manifests itself in the pion cloud.
the pion cloud is a crucial ingredient in the description of the flavor asymmetry, both in the unpolarized and in the polarized distributions.
the flavor asymmetry in the unpolarized case and in the polarized one can be explained by the same physical effect, namely the pion cloud.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of polarized asymmetries, the meson cloud is not a small correction to the quark model, but rather an equally important ingredient.

the flavor asymmetry of polarized antiquark distributions, which is experimentally accessible at JLab, can be used to distinguish between the two mechanisms of antiquark flavor asymmetry in the proton.
the meson cloud is essential for understanding the flavor dependence of the nucleon spin structure.
